question.problem:
Find the Jordan canonical form of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ 1 & 9\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Every $n\times n$ matrix $A$ can be written in the form

$$
A=PJ{P}^{-1},
$$

where $J$ is a Jordan canonical form (or Jordan normal form) of $A,$ and $P$ is an invertible matrix. 

To find the matrix $J,$ we first find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & -1 \\ 1 & 9-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(9-\lambda )-(-1)\cdot 1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-16\lambda +64 & =0 \\ (\lambda -8)(\lambda -8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=8.$ 

Since $A$ is not a scalar matrix, we conclude that $A$ is not diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

$$
J={J}_{2}(8)=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$
